list.item: What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the graph defined by \(y=(x−3)^2+2\)?

solution.para: Correct! 3. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is found by using the squared term of the vertex form. The \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the graph is 3.

list.item: What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of the graph defined by \(y=(x−3)^2+2\)?

solution.para: Correct! 2. In vertex form, the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex is the constant. The value of the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex of the graph is 2.

list.item: Find the coordinates of two other points on the graph. The points should be symmetric across the vertex. Show your reasoning.

problem.para: Write down your answer. Then select the solution button to compare your work.

solution.para: \((0,11)\) and \((6,11)\). When \(x\) is 0, the value of \(y\) is \((-3)^2+2\) or 11. The other point is 3 units to the right of the vertex with the same \(y\)-coordinate.
